chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, who said: Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) was asked
Is it permissible to say that Allah is a Thing? He answered: Yes, it removes Him from the two extremes: the extreme of annulment [ta'til] and the extreme of anthropomorphism [tashbih].
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to call God a 'Thing' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Taqi (AS) clarifies that describing Allah as 'Shay' (a thing/entity) is theologically sound because it serves as a middle path between *Ta'til* (negation of essence) and *Tashbih* (anthropomorphic comparison). This affirmation aligns with the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid al-Sifat*, ensuring that divine attributes are neither denied nor limited to created forms, thereby preserving God's transcendence while affirming His real existence.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqaq (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Kufi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma`il al-Barmaki, on the authority of alHusayn ibn al-Hasan, on the authority of Bakr ibn Salih, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Sa`id that Abu Ja`far the Second (Imam Muhammad al-Taqi (AS) was asked: “
Is it permissible to say that Allah is a Thing? Hence, he (AS) answered: “Yes, to the extent that it removes Him from the two extremes: annulment [ta`til] and anthropomorphism [tashbih].”
